context: the v2 calibration (crowllm_judge_calibration_r11_v2.json) served 20/30 valid with 20/20 correct among valid, but 10 pairs JUDGE_PARSE_FAILED (accuracy 0.667 < 0.8 gate FAIL). This is the bounded one-sample live diagnosis of the parse-failure shape.
method: one live judgment call on eval-new04-chiller-fouling-predictor (a v2 parse-failed pair), raw output inspected; bounded: single call, no large spend

finding.evidence: first-attempt output contained the corrupted token '"B1": .src1' — the free pool injected the literal marker '.src' into a JSON integer value, making the object unparseable (json.loads fails on '.src1'). The engine's ONE parse-retry re-asked and the second attempt returned a complete valid rubric JSON (all keys A1-A6/B1-B6 + prefer).
finding.corruption_class: provider-side (the router's model-serving layer corrupts tokens under free-pool load); NOT a prompt or engine defect — the same prompt parses clean on the retry
finding.recovery_rate: engine parse-retry recovered this sample; 10/30 pairs exhausted the ONE retry with still-corrupt output (or transport-failed the retry) in the v2 run

implication.gate: UNCHANGED — FAIL stands (a parse failure counts as WRONG, Art. XXV; corrupted output is never repaired into a verdict)
implication.candidate_repair_next_session: widen the parse-retry ladder 1x -> 2x for THIS rung only (re-asking is honest — the model re-serves, nothing is guessed or repaired client-side); measured expectation: with corruption bursts clearing in seconds, a second retry should recover a large fraction of the 10; re-run the 30-pair calibration after
